concepts.def: Grouping organisms by similarities to organise life and reflect evolution.
Linnaean groups: animals, plants, fungi, protists, prokaryotes.
Modern division (Woese): bacteria, archaea, eukaryota — based on RNA differences.
Two-part Latin name: Genus species (e.g. Homo sapiens).
Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species (broad → specific).
Group of similar organisms that can interbreed to produce fertile offspring.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Characteristics & Classification — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Characteristics & Classification brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Characteristics & Classification.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
